saints.name: St. Athanasius
saints.title: Bishop and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: The unbending bishop of Alexandria who stood “against the world” for the divinity of Christ through five exiles…
biography: Born at Alexandria about 296, Athanasius became deacon and secretary to Bishop Alexander, whom he accompanied to the Council of Nicaea in 325. There the assembled bishops condemned the teaching of Arius that the Son was a creature, confessing Him instead to be of one being with the Father.

On Alexander's death in 328 Athanasius, barely thirty, was chosen bishop of Alexandria. For forty-five years he defended the Nicene faith, suffering five exiles under four emperors — to Trier, to Rome, and three times into hiding in Egypt — whence the saying Athanasius contra mundum, 'Athanasius against the world'.

In exile and at home he wrote without ceasing: the treatise On the Incarnation, composed in his youth; the Life of Antony, which carried Egyptian monasticism to the West; and the festal letter of 367, the first surviving list of the twenty-seven books of the New Testament.

He died at Alexandria on 2 May 373, and the Council of Constantinople in 381 sealed the faith he had kept. Numbered among the four great Doctors of the Eastern Church, he is honored as patron of theologians, for none labored longer to hand on the apostolic faith entire.
saints.knownFor: His lifelong defense of Christ's divinity against Arianism.

canonization.canonized: Venerated from antiquity; Doctor of the Church

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 2 May
